title: The train enters a slow network
description: A viewer starts at 1080p on fast Wi-Fi, then moves to a slow mobile connection. The catalogue has HLS/DASH renditions whose segments align on the same timestamps. What should adapt playback, and what is the segment-length trade-off?

options.text: The CDN should transcode each cached segment to a smaller resolution when a request is slow.
options.explanation: The CDN serves encoded objects. Per-request transcoding is not the adaptation mechanism in this design.

options.text: The metadata API should choose one bitrate at page load and hold it for the whole video.
options.explanation: A one-time choice cannot react to bandwidth changes during playback.

options.text: The player should keep 1080p and wait for every segment, since aligned renditions are only for seeking.
options.explanation: Alignment enables rendition switches at segment boundaries. Ignoring lower renditions causes avoidable rebuffering.

options.text: The player should choose lower-bitrate next segments from throughput and buffer measurements; shorter segments react faster but add requests and reduce compression efficiency.
options.explanation: The client observes its own network and buffer, so it controls adaptation. Aligned timestamps keep switches continuous; segment duration balances responsiveness, request overhead and compression.
